title: Latency Verdict Board — IO-mode cohorts and model-family breakdown (p50/p95/p99)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Build a single ‘Verdict Board’ that surfaces latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) segmented by model-family and route, with an explicit IO-mode split (streaming vs non‑streaming). The board should make it fast for SRE/Platform/Feature teams to identify whether a tail spike is localized to a particular model family, a set of routes, or the streaming path itself. It must include quick links to representative traces, live KV-cache hit overlays, and an automated ‘verdict’ indicator (OK / Investigate / Critical) computed from SLO breach heuristics.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 for every model-family × route row, with separate sparklines for streaming and non-streaming.
2) Each cell links to a filtered trace view (tracehooks) capturing first-token and last-token timing.
3) A KV-cache-hit overlay toggle displays cache hit-rate histogram aligned with latency sparkline.
4) Automated verdict column computes status using 95th percentile compared against per-route SLOs; clicking verdict opens playbook.
4) Data freshness <= 30s for hosted telemetry and <= 90s for aggregate rollups.
5) Tests: e2e dashboard rendering on staging, unit tests for percentile aggregation, integration test for trace link generation.
6) Dashboard accessible in Console > Observability > Latency Verdicts and included in weekly oncall email when any verdict is Critical.
design_notes:
- Layout: horizontal table with rows by model-family (group models by family tag) and columns by route/endpoint. Each cell contains two tiny sparklines stacked (streaming on top, non-streaming below) + p50/p95/p99 numbers.
- Color scheme: neutral -> amber -> red mapped to % of SLO.
- Trace hooks: embed startOfRequest, firstTokenEmit, lastTokenEmit spans; store span IDs in metric labels to enable quick drill-through.
- Sampling: keep deterministic synthetic sampler for long tail (use shape-based sampling of long-request traces) to ensure reproducible debug sessions.
- Metric naming: use infra.serve.latency.{model_family}.{route}.{io_mode}.{percentile}. Avoid cardinality explosion (roll up model variants under family tag).
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (3 days): metrics pipeline changes to emit model_family and io_mode labels, add percentile rollups (p50/p95/p99) to metrics cluster; add KV cache hit metric join keys.
Phase 2 (5 days): Console UI implementation (table + sparklines + verdict column) + trace link generation.
Phase 3 (2 days): e2e tests, staging rollout, and oncall integration.
Phase 4 (1 day): post-launch monitoring and addressing performance regressions.

review_feedback:
Maya Singh (PM): asked for explicit cell-level SLO target display and a tooltip describing how verdict is computed.
Jonas Karlsson (Design): suggested a compact stacked-sparkline approach and recommended colorblind-friendly palette; also requested microcopy for streaming vs non-streaming.
Talia Gomez (SRE): flagged data freshness constraint; requested that streaming metrics be labeled as approximate during rollbacks.
R&D note (Ravi Patel): prefer family-level aggregation to keep cardinality manageable; may need to drop route-matrix for ultra-high-cardinality routes (apply route sampling).
tradeoffs:
- Cardinality vs fidelity: we avoid emitting per-variant labels to keep TSDB costs down; that means some investigations will require drilling into traces instead of seeing variant-level numbers.
- Freshness vs cost: 30s freshness for hosted telemetry requires more frequent rollups; we implemented an on-write fast-path for streaming metrics to meet this SLA at moderate CPU cost.
- Verdict automation: simple percentile-to-SLO mapping for MVP; more advanced anomaly-detection deferred to a follow-up (observability-ml).

open_questions:
- Do we expose family-level SLOs or require per-route SLO configuration? (PM decision).
- Should KV-cache overlay be on by default or opt-in per user? (UX question).
- If metrics cluster CPU is unstable, do we fall back to coarser rollup intervals for very high-cardinality customers?
notes_for_oncall: When a Verdict becomes Critical: 1) go to the cell and click trace link; 2) check KV-cache overlay for concurrent hit-rate drop; 3) if streaming-only spike, route to streaming-runtime team; 4) if non-streaming spike across families, escalate to infra/serving. See playbook link in Confluence.
postmortem_plan: If an outage is caused by dashboard-driven action (false-positive or missed spike), capture timeline, telemetry ingestion lag, and metric aggregation window. Postmortem owner: Ravi Patel.
